# whose-code-site

> Public case study for whose-code: we scanned 20,245 commits of our own agent-built code with our authorship scanner and published the complete result, warts and all.

whose-code-site is maintained by Adventure Wave Labs (The lab for agentic developer tooling).

## The receipt (method v0.2)

| repo | commits | assisted | machine | unknown | velocity flags | merges w/ review evidence | gate runs | classed w/o confession |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| turbo-rig | 18,282 | 0 | 0 | 18,282 | 0 | 95 / 95 | 370 | 0 |
| ancuria | 1,820 | 37 | 0 | 1,783 | 152 | 102 / 102 | 255 | 0 |
| adventure-wave-explorer | 143 | 0 | 4 | 139 | 0 | 11 / 11 | 33 | 0 |

## The zero, stated precisely

No commit was classified assisted or machine at deciding confidence without a
direct confession — on these repos, under this method. That is what the zero
can prove: indirect signals never decided a class. It is not a general
accuracy guarantee. Classes are assisted / machine / unknown; there is no
"human" class by design — commit messages can prove machine involvement, never
human authorship.
